items.head: Short title, extent and commencement
items.gist: The Limitation Act, 1963. It came into force on 1 January 1964.

items.head: Definitions
items.gist: Defines terms such as applicant, application, bill of exchange, bond, defendant, easement, good faith (done with due care and attention), plaintiff, period of limitation, prescribed period, suit (not including an appeal or application), tort and trustee.

items.head: Bar of limitation
items.gist: Every suit instituted, appeal preferred and application made after the prescribed period is dismissed, even if limitation has not been set up as a defence. A suit is instituted when the plaint is presented; a set-off or counter-claim is treated as a separate suit.

items.head: Expiry when court is closed
items.gist: If the prescribed period expires on a day the court is closed, the suit, appeal or application may be filed on the day the court reopens.

items.head: Extension of period in certain cases
items.gist: An appeal or application (other than under Order XXI CPC) may be admitted after the period if the applicant shows sufficient cause for not filing in time. Does not apply to suits.

items.head: Legal disability
items.gist: If the person entitled to sue is a minor, insane or an idiot when the period begins, he may sue within the same period after the disability ends.

items.head: Disability of one of several persons
items.gist: Where one of several persons jointly entitled is under disability, time does not run against them all until one of them can give a valid discharge without the others' concurrence.

items.head: Special exceptions
items.gist: Sections 6 and 7 do not apply to suits to enforce pre-emption, and do not extend the period beyond three years from the end of the disability or the person's death.

items.head: Continuous running of time
items.gist: Once time has begun to run, no later disability or inability to sue stops it.

items.head: Suits against trustees
items.gist: No period of limitation applies to a suit against a trustee (or his representatives) to follow trust property in his hands for a specific purpose.

items.head: Suits on contracts made outside the territories
items.gist: Suits on foreign contracts are subject to this Act; a foreign limitation rule is no defence unless it extinguishes the contract and the parties were domiciled there throughout.

items.head: Exclusion of time in legal proceedings
items.gist: The day from which the period is reckoned is excluded. For appeals, revision and review, the day of judgment and the time needed to obtain certified copies of the decree, judgment or award are excluded.

items.head: Time spent on indigent applications
items.gist: Where leave to sue or appeal as an indigent person is applied for and rejected, the time spent prosecuting that application in good faith is excluded.

items.head: Proceeding in a court without jurisdiction
items.gist: Time spent prosecuting, with due diligence and in good faith, another civil proceeding in a court which could not entertain it (defect of jurisdiction or similar cause) is excluded.

items.head: Exclusion of time in certain other cases
items.gist: Time during which a suit or execution is stayed by injunction or order is excluded; so is the period of notice required by law before suing (such as S.80 CPC), and certain periods in insolvency and winding-up.

items.head: Effect of death on or before the right to sue accrues
items.gist: Where the person entitled dies before the right to sue accrues, time runs from when there is a legal representative able to sue.

items.head: Effect of fraud or mistake
items.gist: Where the suit is based on the defendant's fraud, or a right is concealed by fraud, or relief is sought from a mistake, time runs from when the plaintiff discovered (or could with reasonable diligence have discovered) the fraud or mistake.

items.head: Effect of acknowledgment in writing
items.gist: A written acknowledgment of liability, signed by the party (or his agent) before the period expires, gives a fresh period from the date it was signed.

items.head: Effect of payment on account of debt
items.gist: Payment on account of a debt or of interest on a legacy, made before the period expires, gives a fresh period from the date of payment (the acknowledgment of payment must be in writing or in the payer's handwriting).

items.head: Acknowledgment or payment by another person
items.gist: An acknowledgment or payment by a duly authorised agent, or by a guardian or manager, has the same effect.

items.head: Substituting or adding a party
items.gist: When a new plaintiff or defendant is added after the suit is filed, the suit is treated, as regards him, as instituted when he was made a party.

items.head: Continuing breaches and torts
items.gist: In a continuing breach of contract or continuing tort, a fresh period begins to run at every moment the breach or tort continues.

items.head: Acts not actionable without special damage
items.gist: For acts not actionable without special damage, time runs from when the injury results.

items.head: Computation of time in instruments
items.gist: Dates and periods in instruments are reckoned by the Gregorian calendar.

items.head: Acquisition of easements by prescription
items.gist: A right of way, light, air or other easement enjoyed peaceably, openly, as of right and without interruption for 20 years becomes absolute (30 years against Government property).

items.head: Exclusion in favour of reversioner
items.gist: Time during which the servient land is held under a life interest or a lease of more than three years is excluded when computing the 20 years, if the reversioner resists within three years of the interest ending.

items.head: Extinguishment of right to property
items.gist: When the period for a suit for possession of any property expires, the owner's right to that property is extinguished.

items.head: Savings
items.gist: Where a special or local law prescribes a different period, that period applies; sections 4 to 24 apply to it unless expressly excluded.

items.head: Suits with shorter periods than under the 1908 Act
items.gist: Transitional provision for suits whose period became shorter under this Act than under the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.

items.head: Barred or pending suits
items.gist: Nothing in this Act revives a right already barred under the 1908 Act, or affects suits pending at commencement.

items.head: Balance due on a mutual, open and current account
items.gist: 3 years — from the close of the year in which the last item is entered.

items.head: Price of goods sold and delivered (no fixed credit period)
items.gist: 3 years — from the date of delivery.

items.head: Price of work done (no time fixed for payment)
items.gist: 3 years — from when the work is done.

items.head: Money lent or paid
items.gist: 3 years — from when the loan is made.

items.head: Money lent, payable on demand
items.gist: 3 years — from when the loan is made.

items.head: Money deposited, payable on demand (including with a bank)
items.gist: 3 years — from when the demand is made.

items.head: Money paid under a mistake
items.gist: 3 years — from when the mistake becomes known.

items.head: Specific performance of a contract
items.gist: 3 years — from the date fixed for performance, or if none, from when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused.

items.head: Compensation for breach of contract
items.gist: 3 years — from when the contract is broken (or the breach ceases, for successive or continuing breaches).

items.head: Any other declaration
items.gist: 3 years — from when the right to sue first accrues.

items.head: Cancel or set aside an instrument or decree, or rescind a contract
items.gist: 3 years — from when the facts entitling the plaintiff to that relief first become known to him.

items.head: Possession of immovable property based on previous possession (not title)
items.gist: 12 years — from the date of dispossession.

items.head: Possession of immovable property based on title
items.gist: 12 years — from when the defendant's possession becomes adverse to the plaintiff.

items.head: Compensation for an act or omission under an enactment
items.gist: 1 year — from when the act or omission takes place.

items.head: Compensation for false imprisonment
items.gist: 1 year — from when the imprisonment ends.

items.head: Compensation for malicious prosecution
items.gist: 1 year — from when the plaintiff is acquitted or the prosecution is otherwise terminated.

items.head: Compensation for libel
items.gist: 1 year — from when the libel is published.

items.head: Compensation for slander
items.gist: 1 year — from when the words are spoken, or the special damage results if not actionable without it.

items.head: Any suit by or on behalf of the Central or a State Government
items.gist: 30 years — from when the period would begin to run against a like suit by a private person.

items.head: Any suit for which no period is provided elsewhere
items.gist: 3 years — from when the right to sue accrues.

items.head: Appeal from an order of acquittal
items.gist: 90 days from the order (State's appeal); 30 days from the grant of special leave (other appeals against acquittal).

items.head: Appeal from a sentence
items.gist: Death sentence: 30 days. Other sentences: 60 days to the High Court, 30 days to any other court.

items.head: Appeal under the Code of Civil Procedure
items.gist: 90 days to a High Court; 30 days to any other court — from the date of the decree or order.

items.head: Appeal from a High Court decree or order to the same High Court
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of the decree or order.

items.head: Leave to appear and defend a summary suit
items.gist: 10 days — from when the summons is served.

items.head: To bring legal representatives on record
items.gist: 90 days — from the date of death of the plaintiff, appellant, defendant or respondent.

items.head: To set aside an abatement
items.gist: 60 days — from the date of abatement.

items.head: To restore a suit or appeal dismissed for default
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of dismissal.

items.head: To set aside an ex parte decree or rehear an appeal heard ex parte
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of the decree, or from when the applicant knew of it where summons was not duly served.

items.head: Review of judgment (by a court other than the Supreme Court)
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of the decree or order.

items.head: To set aside a sale in execution
items.gist: 60 days — from the date of the sale.

items.head: Decree-holder or purchaser resisted in getting possession
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of resistance or obstruction.

items.head: Person dispossessed in execution, disputing the right to possession
items.gist: 30 days — from the date of dispossession.

items.head: Leave to appeal as an indigent person
items.gist: 60 days to a High Court; 30 days to any other court.

items.head: Revision
items.gist: 90 days — from the date of the decree or order.

items.head: Certificate for appeal to the Supreme Court
items.gist: 60 days — from the date of the decree, order or sentence.

items.head: Delivery of possession to a purchaser at an execution sale
items.gist: 1 year — from when the sale becomes absolute.

items.head: Execution of a decree or order
items.gist: 12 years — from when the decree becomes enforceable. A decree for a mandatory injunction has no limit.

items.head: Any other application
items.gist: 3 years — from when the right to apply accrues.
